checks.label: A function is a rule which operates on an input and produces a single output from that input: on the transmitter, tank, workshop and tariff graphs the beam up from every input meets the graph once, and only the pipe's rim gives one input two outputs
If there is a 12 mA signal from the DP cell, that is 50% DP: the beam back from 12 mA meets the transmitter's line once and comes down at 50%

Each real-world value is converted into its analog current equivalent with the linear equation y = mx + b: the transmitter's graph is one straight line, rising by the same amount for every equal step across

A horizontal line drawn on the graph cuts it more than once, so two different inputs have yielded the same output and the function is many-to-one: the level line back from the tank's level, and from the workshop's temperature, meets each graph twice, and both inputs it finds give that same output

Every worked number is right: 25% reads 8 mA; 75% reads 16 mA against the slips 12 mA (counted from 4 mA) and 20 mA (the line's end); back from 12 mA is 50%; back from 18 mA is 87.5% against 112.5% (18 ÷ 0.16, leaving out the 4 mA) and 18%; the tank is at 1 m at 5 min, falls from 2 m at 20 min to 0 at 30 min, and is at 1 m again at 25 min; the workshop is at 22 °C at 10:00 and 20:00 and at 25 °C at 12:00 and 17:00; the rim is 4 and −4 cm up at 3 cm across and 3 and −3 cm at 4 cm, as 3² + 4² = 5²; the tariff is 10p before 07:00 and 30p from 07:00; and back from 10 mA is 37.5%, as 0.16 × 37.5 + 4 = 10
Before Check a puzzle draws no reading; a right answer draws the reading it names and nothing in red, and each wrong answer draws its own slip in red, with the slip's value where it names one

Every dot a beam lands on sits on its graph at its place, and every value written on an axis is that dot's own reading: on each puzzle's answers, each opening demonstration, and every place Dan can drag a pointer to
Every demonstration has finished arriving within its 3.2 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
